props.statement: The default managed-memory path closes the state handler before stopping Beam requests, which can cause IllegalStateException during shutdown callbacks.

statement.value: The default managed-memory path closes the state handler before stopping Beam requests, which can cause IllegalStateException during shutdown callbacks.

n_5d22a4ec55b2351aa9e8d90fe09c2643.value: The default managed-memory path closes the state handler before stopping Beam requests. Managed mode stores JobBundleFactory only in a local variable and is enabled by default. Consequently, close() gates stateRequestHandler before releasing sharedResources; the actual shared factory closes afterward—or remains active until the final lease. Shutdown callbacks can therefore receive IllegalStateException

props.title: Managed memory path closes state handler prematurely

props.statement: Shutdown must drain requests before closing the state handler to avoid IllegalStateException.

props.statement: The inferRowType() method in SqlWindowTableFunction.java incorrectly preserves the ROWTIME attribute on the original time column instead of materializing it to a regular TIMESTAMP.

statement.value: The inferRowType() method in SqlWindowTableFunction.java incorrectly preserves the ROWTIME attribute on the original time column instead of materializing it to a regular TIMESTAMP.

n_2ac5713ebbc0ab45cb7754e58842e921.value: This method constructs the output schema of all window TVFs (TUMBLE/HOP/CUMULATE) via ARG0_TABLE_FUNCTION_WINDOWING. It uses .addAll(inputRowType.getFieldList()) to copy all input fields into the output, which blindly preserves the TimeIndicatorRelDataType (ROWTIME) on the original time column instead of materializing it to a regular TIMESTAMP.

props.statement: Mini-batch aggregation caches input records in a buffer to reduce state access overhead, trading latency for throughput.

n_3eb763ae27408d54dbe75f9d518bfb3d.value: The core idea of mini-batch aggregation is caching a bundle of inputs in a buffer inside of the aggregation operator. When the bundle of inputs is triggered to process, only one operation per key to access state is needed. This can significantly reduce the state overhead and get a better throughput. However, this may increase some latency because it buffers some records instead of processing them in an instant.
